call.title: Runbook — PostgreSQL stops writing when the disk is full
call.content:
Runbook — PostgreSQL stops writing when the disk is full
4 steps, from the chat "db1 disk full"

## When to use
The shop shows "could not write" errors; `journalctl -u postgresql` says "No space left on device".

## Steps
1. `df -h /var/lib/pg` — confirm the disk is at 100%.
2. `sudo du -sh /var/log/postgresql/*` — find the old logs.
3. `sudo find /var/log/postgresql -name '*.log.*' -mtime +7 -delete` — remove logs older than a week.
4. `sudo systemctl restart postgresql` — restart.

## Verify
1. "100%" in the Use column. 2. a file over 1G. 3. `df -h` under 90%. 4. `SELECT 1` answers.

## Rollback
- nothing to undo; the logs removed were rotated copies.

## Escalate
- if `df` is still over 90% after step 3, stop: the data folder itself is full; call the person who wrote this. Deleting WAL files does not help and loses data.

Postmortem — orders down on 9 Nov

## Actions
- Add a disk alert at 85% on db1: `sudo apt install monit`, then write /etc/monit/conf.d/disk with `check filesystem pg with path /mnt/fast if space usage > 85% then alert`, then `sudo monit reload`.

call.title: Runbook — disk alert on db1
call.content:
Runbook — disk alert on db1
3 steps, from the document "Postmortem — orders down on 9 Nov"

## When to use
Setting up the disk alert on db1 the postmortem asked for, or checking it is still there.

## Steps
1. `sudo apt install monit` — install the monitor.
2. `sudo tee /etc/monit/conf.d/disk` with `check filesystem pg with path /mnt/fast if space usage > 85% then alert` — the rule.
3. `sudo monit reload` — load it.

## Verify
1. `monit --version` answers. 2. the file reads back. 3. `sudo monit status` lists pg.

## Rollback
- `sudo rm /etc/monit/conf.d/disk && sudo monit reload`.

## Escalate
- if monit status does not list pg after step 3, stop and read /var/log/monit.log; reinstalling does not help.
